variables.claim_asserts: The rules for generating primes are simple, yet their distribution seems in many respects random. The historical remark that mathematics neglected this is part of the recorded statement and is not the mathematical claim.
variables.test_measures: Seven pre-registered statistics on primes below 10^8, each compared with a threshold and calibrated on one Cramer-model simulation (seed 20261031). Random-like in 3 of 7: R2 consecutive-gap correlation −0.0349 (threshold |rho| < 0.05), R3 residue shares coprime to 12 (max deviation 5.9e-5, threshold 0.005), R7 max |pi(x)−Li(x)| / sqrt(x/ln x) = 1.269 (threshold < 3). Not random-like: R1 coarse gap-CDF deviation 0.0363 (threshold 0.03), R4 Poisson total variation 0.0776 (threshold 0.02), R5 Fourier max/mean power 87606 (threshold < 30; peak period 3), R6 lzma size versus a shuffle 0.9617 (threshold >= 0.98). Refutes if random-like in at most 3 of 7 calibrated respects. The sieve matches OEIS A000040 (first 10000) and pi(10^8) = 5761455.

modality.note: The claim is about the distribution of primes generated by a simple rule. A sieve of Eratosthenes up to 10^8, checked against the OEIS prime list and pi(10^8), is that sequence. Cramer's model (independent inclusion with probability 1/ln n) is the declared random comparison, and the simulation itself passes all seven thresholds, so the cutoffs are calibrated.

assumptions.note: 'Seems in many respects random' is not a list of numerical tolerances. interpretation states the operational reading (indistinguishability from a random model in a majority of a fixed list) and states that the list includes respects where structure is already known, including Fourier peaks from small moduli, so that the test can fail. R5's period-3 peak is that sieve regularity; it is one of the four failures, and the plainly-regular trigger (raw lzma ratio < 0.1, or one frequency carrying more than half the power) does not fire (raw ratio 0.553, peak share 0.042). The criterion is stricter than 'seems', and the caveats note that R1 < 0.05 and R6 >= 0.95 would give 5 of 7 and support. That is a declared tightening of the same variable, not a different distribution.

scope.claim_scope: The distribution of the prime numbers, said to seem random in many respects, as an instance of complexity from simple rules.
scope.test_scope: Primes below 10^8. Gap, interval and compression statistics use [5×10^7, 10^8]; the Fourier test uses 2^22 odd numbers just below 10^8. Seven respects. The remark about what mathematics neglected is excluded, as interpretation says.

reasons: The measured object is the prime distribution against a declared random model. Three respects meet the random-like thresholds (gaps' consecutive correlation, residues coprime to 12, the scaled pi(x)−Li(x) fluctuation) and four do not. Scoring 'many respects' as at least 5 of 7 for support and at most 3 of 7 for refutation is a narrowing to one battery, stated in advance, on one finite range.

The refutation is threshold-sensitive inside that battery. R1 misses 0.03 by 0.006 and R6 misses 0.98 by about 0.018; both are the same small-gap and consecutive-gap structure. R4 (Fano factor 0.762, Poisson TV 0.078) and R5 (period 3, max/mean ~8.8×10^4 versus 15.5 under Cramer) are larger departures. Counting R5 against the claim is the weakest part of the criterion, because interpretation says the book already treats that modular peak as a regularity. It is still a respect of the prime distribution, and it is not the sole failure.

The simple generating rule is the sieve, which is what the quote contrasts with the distribution. The historical clause is not measured. That omission is stated, so the verdict speaks only to the distributional sentence, on this range and this list.
what_would_change_it: Dropping respects the text already treats as regularities (the period-3 Fourier peak) from the fail count, and setting the gap-CDF and compression cutoffs at the scale of 'seems' rather than at 0.03 and 0.98, would match the wording more closely; the caveats say the looser pair of cutoffs would support. A test aimed at the historical remark, or at a single modular regularity alone, would be about something other than 'in many respects random'.
